# Song of Solomon Chapter 2 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**2:1** I [ani] [am] a-rose [chavatzelet] of-Sharon [ha-Sharon], a-lily [shoshannat] of-the-valleys [ha-amaqim].

**2:2** Like-a-lily [ke-shoshannah] among the-thorns [bein ha-chochim], so [ken] [is] my-darling [ra'yati] among the-daughters [bein ha-banot].

**2:3** Like-an-apple-tree [ke-tappuach] among the-trees [ba-atzei] of-the-forest [ha-ya'ar], so [ken] [is] my-beloved [dodi] among the-sons [bein ha-banim]. In-his-shade [be-tzillo] I-delighted [chimmadti] and-I-sat [ve-yashavti], and-his-fruit [u-firyo] [was] sweet [matoq] to-my-palate [le-chikki].

**2:4** He-brought-me [hevi'ani] to the-house [el beit] of-wine [ha-yayin], and-his-banner [ve-diglo] over-me [alai] [was] love [ahavah].

**2:5** Sustain-me [sammekhuni] with-raisin-cakes [ba-ashishot], refresh-me [rappduni] with-apples [ba-tappuchim], for I [ki] [am] sick [cholat] of-love [ahavah].

**2:6** His-left [smo'lo] [hand is] under my-head [tachat le-roshi], and-his-right [vi-mino] embraces-me [techabbeqeni].

**2:7** I-adjure-you [hishba'ti etkhem], daughters [benot] of-Jerusalem [Yerushalayim], by-the-gazelles [bi-tzeva'ot] or by-the-does [o be-aylot] of-the-field [ha-sadeh]: do-not-stir [im ta'iru] and-do-not-awaken [ve-im te'oreru] love [et ha-ahavah] until [ad] she-pleases [she-techpatz].

**2:8** The-voice [qol] of-my-beloved [dodi]! Behold [hinneh], he-comes [zeh ba], leaping [medalleg] upon the-mountains [al he-harim], bounding [meqappetz] upon the-hills [al ha-geva'ot].

**2:9** My-beloved [dodi] is-like [domeh] a-gazelle [li-tzevi] or a-young [le-ofer] stag [ha-ayyalim]. Behold [hinneh zeh], he-stands [omed] behind our-wall [achar kotlenu], gazing [mashgiach] through the-windows [min ha-challonot], peering [metzitz] through the-lattice [min ha-charakkim].

**2:10** My-beloved [dodi] answered [anah] and-said [ve-amar] to-me [li]: "Arise [qumi], my-darling [ra'yati], my-beautiful-one [yafati], and-come-away [u-lekhi lakh].

**2:11** For behold [ki hinneh], the-winter [ha-setav] has-passed [avar], the-rain [ha-geshem] is-over [chalaf] [and] gone [halakh lo].

**2:12** The-blossoms [ha-nitzanim] have-appeared [nir'u] in-the-land [ba-aretz], the-time [et] of-singing [ha-zamir] has-arrived [higgi'a], and-the-voice [ve-qol] of-the-turtledove [ha-tor] is-heard [nishma] in-our-land [be-artzenu].

**2:13** The-fig-tree [ha-te'enah] has-ripened [chantah] its-early-figs [faggeha], and-the-vines [ve-ha-gepanim] [in] blossom [semadar] give [natnu] fragrance [re'ach]. Arise [qumi], my-darling [lakh ra'yati], my-beautiful-one [yafati], and-come-away [u-lekhi lakh]."

**2:14** My-dove [yonati] in-the-clefts [be-chagvei] of-the-rock [ha-sela], in-the-hiding-place [be-seter] of-the-cliff [ha-madregah], show-me [har'ini] your-appearance [et mar'ayikh], let-me-hear [hashmi'ini] your-voice [et qolekh]; for your-voice [ki qolekh] [is] sweet [arev], and-your-appearance [u-mar'ekh] [is] lovely [naveh].

**2:15** Catch [ichzu] for-us [lanu] foxes [shu'alim], little [qetannim] foxes [shu'alim] that-ruin [mechabbelim] vineyards [keramim]; and-our-vineyards [u-kheramenu] [are in] blossom [semadar].

**2:16** My-beloved [dodi] [is] mine [li] and-I [va-ani] [am] his [lo]; he-pastures [ha-ro'eh] among-the-lilies [ba-shoshannim].

**2:17** Until [ad] the-day [she-yafuach ha-yom] breathes and-the-shadows [ve-ha-tzelalim] flee [nasu], turn [sov], be-like [demeh lekha dodi], my-beloved, a-gazelle [li-tzevi] or a-young [le-ofer] stag [ha-ayyalim] upon the-mountains [al harei] of-Bether [bater].

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "rose of Sharon" (chavatzelet ha-Sharon):** The Hebrew *chavatzelet* is not a rose but likely a crocus, narcissus, or meadow saffron. Sharon is the coastal plain between Joppa and Carmel — fertile lowland. The woman identifies herself not with rare flowers but with common wildflowers.

**v.7 — The adjuration formula:** "By the gazelles and does of the field" — the Hebrew *tzeva'ot* (gazelles) puns on *Tzeva'ot* (Hosts, as in "LORD of Hosts"), and *aylot* (does) puns on *El* (God). The oath formula avoids direct divine names while echoing them.

**v.12 — "the time of singing" (et ha-zamir):** The word *zamir* means both "singing" (of birds) and "pruning" (of vines). Both meanings fit the springtime context.

*-- EMET*
